summary: Ruth Norton Albright (1892–1979) was an Indologist. She studied under Maurice Bloomfield and completed her PhD at Johns Hopkins University in 1921.

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi (1987–1988), and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.
Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He completed an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University, studying under Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Tenpa Gyaltsen, L. S. Summer, Jirka Hladis, and traditional teachers Tsultrim Allione, Gochen Tulku Sang-ngag Rinpoche, and Urgyen Wangchuk.

Ryan Richard Overbey is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Brown (AB 1997–2001) and Harvard (PhD 2001–2010). His posts include Skidmore College (2017), UC Berkeley (2013–2015), Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, College of the Holy Cross, and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).
Ryo Kuroiwa is a researcher in computational studies and Indology. He has held appointments at the National Institute of Informatics and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Ryo Nishimura (1972–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1995) and under Fumihiko Sueki (~1996–2004).
Ryōshō Taira (1906–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He was affiliated with Taisho University, where he is attested as professor emeritus in 1976 and held a post attested in 1984.
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has held positions as a full-time lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015–2026) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara (1909–2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1939–1943). He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin and served as professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1974).
Ryoichi Kondo (1930–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He was a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later served as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryoji Kishino works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Ryojin Soga (1875–1971) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, and Kōkōdō under Manshi Kiyozawa. He was a professor at Toyo University (1916–1924) and held professorships, emeritus status (1951), and the presidency (1961–1967) at Otani University.

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryokei Kaginushi (1926–2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters (attested 1978) and professor (attested 1993) at Otani University.
Ryoken Nawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2020–2026).
Ryoko Mochizuki (born 1933) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1963) and worked as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1972 and 1983).

Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872–1946) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz and Alfred Foucher, and held teaching posts at Ryukoku University (1897), Third Higher School (1899), and Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate at Toyo University in 1993. He became professor (1973) and professor emeritus (2007) at Taisho University, visiting professor at Shuchiin University (2012), and director at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

Ryoshin Nakao (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1989–2018) and as a member of the Research Institute of Soto Studies.
